intro: Luna 17 landed in Mare Imbrium on November 17, 1970 — and deployed Lunokhod 1, the first wheeled vehicle to operate on another world, beating NASA's LRV by seven months. Lunokhod 1 drove 10.5 km over 11 lunar days, controlled by a five-person team in Crimea. Returned 25,000 photographs and 211 panoramas before going silent in September 1971.

images.caption: Lunokhod 1 — 8-wheeled, 756 kg, solar-powered chassis with a polonium-210 RTG for nighttime warmth. Designed for 3 months, lasted 10.
Luna 17 lander + ramps for Lunokhod 1 deployment. The Soviet remote-control team operated from a converted submarine on the Crimean coast.
Lunokhod 1 driving on Mare Imbrium — controlled by a five-person team in real time despite the 2.5 second light-speed delay each way.
Lunokhod 1 traverse map — 10.5 km zigzag across Mare Imbrium, with science stops at rocks and craters.
Lunokhod 1 retroreflector — still used by Earth-based lunar-laser-ranging stations today, 50+ years later.
